chapter: Thomas, own bands and neighborhood clubs
title: How he came to record, and the Home Inn
summary: Two collectors asked him to record while he worked at the Home Inn; he describes building up a small club.

people.name: Lawrence (trumpet player in Barnes's small-club bands)

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Yeah. Well how did you come to make those records when you had that all come about?
Well they come about just to ask me would I make them.
Did you know them before you made the record? No. No at all. Did they come to the place you were playing at?
They came up there, yeah. Came up last night to record. I was gonna make a recording.
What was the club you were working at then?
I was, I think I was at the Home Inn.
You were there a long time?
When I'm around, I stop in, see, in the town, you know all the things crazy about me.

I started to play some of the little schoolroom house like this. Just like this house, straight up. Started dancing there, playing there. I had a time, they couldn't pay me. Me and my trumpet player lost. We take the drop. And all the jewels. Could buy, drink, and pay them. I know my tribe was playing drum with us, at the bass. And this girl Alma was playing piano.

Alma, I don't know how her last name is. But now she was playing piano, the piano player. So they just paid me and Lawrence with me to get nickels too. We'd be satisfied. Continue waiting, waiting, waiting, waiting, waiting. One company in the place. One nice time, two, three in about three weeks after. Little gang sitting around. We started building.
Increased until the place got back at this now. Is that right? Did you play at that place when it was as big as it is now? I played there, yeah. Because it's now.
Which I can't play there now if I want. Man, if I was going to tell them I want to play here, I'm sorry for the band there. Got to go.
